title: This Bird Stands Motionless for Hours, Then Falls on Its Prey

scenes.text: This bird waits for hours without moving.
The shoebill. Up to five feet tall, with a foot-long bill that looks like a Dutch clog.
It stands in African swamps, frozen. Not a feather moves. Lungfish rise to breathe, right beside it.
Then it doesn't strike. It collapses forward, falling on its prey with the whole bill open.
The edges are razor sharp and the tip is a hook. It takes lungfish, eels, snakes and baby crocodiles.
Fewer than 5,300 adults are left. A bird that patient is hard to replace.

description:
The shoebill of East African swamps stays motionless for hours, then lunges or collapses forward onto prey with a foot-long, hooked bill.
Its menu includes lungfish, eels, snakes and baby crocodiles, and the IUCN estimates only 3,300 to 5,300 adults remain.
Would you have the patience to stand still for hours?
thumbnail_text: STILL FOR HOURS. THEN IT FALLS.
subject: shoebill bird
first_comment: It can wait for hours for one meal. What is the most patient animal you know?
